assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:anju-emma@original-light-novels#86-anju-emma-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-4 Anju Emma character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels V01-V14, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental ordinary-life evidence and Alter.2 excluded. The project's Character Modeling Reference method (its purpose and Japanese-voice sections) was read for method and authority order only. The CMR-9 profile gate audit row and the profile's validation report are not curated evidence on this subject, and no count, version or verdict is taken from them. The ledgers L01, L02 and L09, Documents 04, 08 and 09, the relationship matrix, the diagnostic index, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its HIGH, MODERATE and OPEN labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume, Alter.2 scene or other character's profile is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's phases from V01 (concealed injury, ordinary tenderness and delayed grief) through V14 (fear without disqualification). V05 is split at the scar recognition (p-005 ¶752) and the refusal of romance (¶771-782); V09 at the admission that Daiya, her dead comrade, remains loved while Dustin can be loved differently, and the reciprocal return promise (p-006 ¶493-506); V13 at the overresponsible offer (p-005 ¶126), the breakdown with Kurena (Kurena Kukumila) (p-005 ¶667-685), the retaliatory crisis and its interruption (p-006 ¶151-183) and the reunion (p-007 ¶587-605); and V14 at the mental-disruption impairment (p-006 ¶214; p-007 ¶256) and the fight through fear (p-008 ¶260-428). V02-V04, V05-V07, V08-V09 and V11-V12 are otherwise grouped phases. The V10 rows are Sector-memory scenes from before V01, not a V10 state. No default state is set; one must be selected. Alter.1 rows are ordinary-life supplements without volume placement, and states after V14 are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a causal account of Anju (Anju Emma): her composure is chosen regulation of what she displays according to what the people around her need, not low affect (V12 p-005 ¶519; V01 p-012 ¶89, ¶186), and her care turns pain into material arrangements. It states two sequences: under ordinary stress she notices, regulates her own display, makes a practical adjustment and speaks briefly; under severe grief or threat she contains, keeps functioning, accumulates, and then breaks into embodied rupture, self-condemnation or a retaliatory impulse, which ends in interruption or later release. It says what changes her response: whether someone is unilaterally absorbing risk (anger at Shin (Shinei Nouzen), V02 p-005 ¶98, ¶317), whether others currently depend on her stability, whether romantic attention is unexpected (V05 p-005 ¶771-776), which context a memory of Daiya, her dead comrade, activates, and whether a beloved person is in danger. It predicts her mistakes: overresponsibility that takes authorship of Dustin's burden (V13 p-004 ¶200; p-005 ¶126), self-condemnation as a 'witch' (V13 p-006 ¶151), and retaliatory narrowing toward a human attacker (p-006 ¶161), with the located self-recognition (¶171) and interruption (¶180). A would overclaim: the set is one derived artifact that defers to L01, L02 and L09 outside it, the retaliatory crisis is sampled once and was ended by an order, T14-OQ-24 stays open, and how often she asks for care outside the Dustin relation is only MODERATE. C would understate an account that discriminates risk, dependence, surprise, memory context and danger and predicts her overreach with its corrections.

The profile gives an ordered developmental account of Anju (Anju Emma) with located turning points: V01 concealment and delayed release (p-012 ¶85-89, ¶186); V02 a military return that imagining Daiya, her dead comrade, alive does not change (p-006 ¶150); V05 the scar recognition (p-005 ¶752) and the anti-romance rule (¶771-782); V07 scar treatment begun (p-009 ¶98); V08 non-reconciliation with her father (p-004 ¶234-236); V09 additive attachment and the reciprocal return promise to Dustin (p-006 ¶493-506); V12 composure stated as a choice (p-005 ¶519); V13 overresponsibility, breakdown, retaliatory crisis and reunion (p-005 ¶126-685; p-006 ¶151-183; p-007 ¶333-605); and V14 temporary impairment and fighting through fear (p-006 ¶214; p-007 ¶256; p-008 ¶260-428). It forbids reading later states as erasing earlier ones: Daiya stays loved, scar treatment is not resolution, and composure after V13 does not end the crisis. C would understate located, causally ordered transitions with these controls. A is rejected: V02-V04, V05-V07, V08-V09 and V11-V12 are grouped phases; V03, V06, V09 and V11 have four to five rows each; the V10 rows are Sector memories rather than a V10 state; no default state is named; and nothing after V14 is established.

The profile fixes Anju's (Anju Emma's) first person as 私, describes her ordinary speech as controlled, feminine and socially smooth, gives her relational address set (シン君, セオ君, クレナちゃん, フレデリカちゃん, ダスティン君, ダイヤ君) and the negotiated first-name shift (もうアンジュでいいわよ。同い年でしょ, V05 p-005 ¶696), and states four state rules: calm wording can carry anger (V02 p-005 ¶317); unexpected romantic attention breaks her fluency (V05 p-005 ¶771-776; V13 p-003 ¶166); vulnerability simplifies into short direct requests (私をおいては死なないって、言ってくれたわね, V09 p-006 ¶486; 帰ってきて、──ダスティン君, V13 p-007 ¶336); and humor can be dry or taunting (ようこそお馬鹿さん, V14 p-008 ¶260). D would understate a located first-person and address system with state deltas. B would overclaim: the profile itself calls her voice 'low-friction social calibration' rather than particular forms, and gives no sentence-ending, second-person or politeness distribution, no rule for when she uses polite or plain forms with whom, and no command-form exemplar, all fields the project's own method asks for where supported; its 38 would-sound-wrong constraints are mostly about content rather than form; address toward Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) and other superiors is not given; and the L09 voice ledger is outside the set.

The profile treats ordinary life as central for Anju (Anju Emma) and says what drives it: care converts an abstract future into material arrangements (coffee, food, clothing, birthdays, flowers); aesthetic attention is future-bearing (the backless dresses and bikinis she wants, and scar treatment, V07 p-009 ¶98); and the ordinary-stress sequence (notice, regulate display, adjust practically, speak briefly) predicts what she does when a peer is overworking. Located ordinary conduct runs across the corpus: coffee for the group and a check on Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (V01 p-007 ¶375-404), lace (V01 p-008 ¶18), cooking classes (V02 p-006 ¶77), Sector-memory breakfast, laundry, flower-dyed nails and the bath project (V10 p-025 ¶24; p-027 ¶24-188), study coaching for Kurena (Kurena Kukumila) (V12 p-004 ¶163-166), a romance film (V12 p-004 ¶308), requisition rules that spare private homes and recipe talk (V14 p-004 ¶288-301, ¶616), and the Alter.1 kitten care, war-shaped 'small walk', gifts and dried-flower bouquet. C would understate stated drivers with located conduct and a prediction for ordinary peer settings. A is rejected: there is no routine, sequence or frequency, the Alter.1 rows are not placed by volume, the V10 rows are memories of the Sector, and several listed tastes (potpourri, social drinking) rest on one row or none.

Directed relations from Anju (Anju Emma) are analyzed and distinguished: Daiya, her dead comrade, as living history and later ethical memory (V01 p-012 ¶86; Alter.1 part0014); Dustin, from practical peer and thrown sparring partner (V04 p-006 ¶298-314) through guarded refusal (V05 p-005 ¶771-782) and additive attachment with a reciprocal return promise (V09 p-006 ¶493-506) to the V13 conflict and return (p-005 ¶126-150; p-007 ¶333-605); Kurena (Kurena Kukumila) as a peer she protects who later supports her (V13 p-005 ¶685); Shin (Shinei Nouzen) as a family-like peer whose unilateral risk angers her (V02 p-005 ¶98, ¶317); Theo (Theoto Rikka), whom she corrects (V01 p-008 ¶295) and welcomes back (V14 p-005 ¶133); Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), under warm care with a hard boundary (V11 p-014 ¶129); Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and the female peer network; and subordinates in concise command. C would understate this partner-specific discrimination. A is rejected: Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) and Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) rest on one row each; superiors are sampled only in the V13 staff-officer interruption and the V14 praise from Grethe; Daiya appears alive only in Alter.1 and memory; and the relationship matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Anju's (Anju Emma's) private states are located at several points: suppressed tears in the shower with Kurena (Kurena Kukumila) (V01 p-012 ¶89); inability to picture a postwar 'after' (V08 p-006 ¶49); the self-revision that Daiya, her dead comrade, remains loved, that the claim that Dustin cannot be loved is false, and that she may be using Daiya as an excuse to stay still (V09 p-006 ¶493-504); the belief that her request cursed Dustin (V13 p-006 ¶151); recognition that she may be turning a person into a target for her rage (¶171); the thought that she wanted Daiya beside her and now wants Dustin back beside her (p-007 ¶333); the survivor's belief after battle (¶544); and narrated fear of the mental-disruption enemy (V14 p-008 ¶262). These states drive located choices: the return promise, the request to come back, lowering the weapon and fighting while afraid. C would understate rendered interior logic causally linked to conduct. A is rejected: exemplars are not classified as dialogue, inner speech or focalized narration; V02-V07 interior is thin and the V05 refusal is spoken; the V12 composure statement is spoken disclosure to Shin (Shinei Nouzen); and T14-OQ-24 leaves the mature form of her memory and attachment open.

The profile states Anju's (Anju Emma's) conflict classes and what shifts them: at baseline she narrows conflict through a boundary, a quiet correction or silence; with intimates she is blunter; when another person unilaterally absorbs risk she becomes openly angry while her wording stays smooth (V02 p-005 ¶98, ¶317); she corrects a grieving Theo (Theoto Rikka) without denying his grievance (V01 p-008 ¶295); she holds a non-negotiable protective boundary with Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) behind a smile (V11 p-014 ¶129); and under severe grief she moves quickly into self-condemnation or retaliatory judgment (V13 p-005 ¶667; p-006 ¶151-161). It separates obeying the order to lower the weapon and recognizing the moral problem (p-006 ¶171-180) from defending the impulse, and shows a command decision that does not simply follow Dustin (p-006 ¶486). C would understate conditioned response families with a located crisis form. A is rejected: the retaliatory crisis is sampled once and ended by a staff officer's order, conflict with superiors is otherwise unsampled, physical conflict outside combat is comic sparring, and what would stop her without interruption in a new crisis is stated as a possibility, not a tested rule.

The profile gives Anju (Anju Emma) a reasoning style, preferring choices she can morally inhabit afterward and attending to what a decision does to the person who makes it, and locates argued positions: imagining Daiya, her dead comrade, alive does not change what she wants and ought to do (V02 p-006 ¶150); non-reconciliation with her father is a legitimate boundary aimed at making his memory ordinary (V08 p-004 ¶234-236); partiality and 'a little selfishness' are permitted against martyrdom (V11 p-010 ¶218-232; V12 p-008 ¶453); care can become coercive authorship over Dustin (V13 p-004 ¶200; p-005 ¶126); the retaliatory temptation and its recognition (V13 p-006 ¶161-183); and requisition that spares private homes for returning residents (V14 p-004 ¶301). It predicts the failure mode of judging herself more harshly than the situation warrants. C would understate located positions with a reasoning style and failure modes. A is rejected: the competing-duty weighing in V13 is sampled once and resolved by an order, her political judgment of the Republic is limited to not equating ancestry with guilt and not requiring forgiveness, and no postwar ethical choice is modeled.

The profile names the source of Anju's (Anju Emma's) comedy as the contrast between serene presentation and sharp action and lists located forms: deadpan fake concern for Daiya, her dead comrade (V01 p-007 ¶144; Alter.1 part0014 ¶11); suppressed laughter (V02 p-007 ¶116); an off-beat 馬鹿なの!? (V03 p-009 ¶68); tackling and throwing peers (V04 p-005 ¶342; p-006 ¶303-314); mischievous teasing of Dustin's dancing (V07 p-009 ¶89); open laughter in operational banter (V12 p-007 ¶521); a taunt through terror (V14 p-008 ¶260); and Alter.1 birthday pranks in callsign language (part0053 ¶8-25). It says she can be the instigator, not only the straight woman. B would overclaim: the section does not say when her humor is suspended or when teasing wounds, its only functional statement is the contrast, and much of the material is Alter.1 without volume placement. D would understate located forms across V01-V14 and Alter.1 with a stated source.

A dedicated canonical profile of Anju (Anju Emma) over V01-V14 with Alter.1 supplemental and 139 routed diagnostic rows with EPUB paragraph routes, 127 in V01-V14 and 12 in Alter.1; the profile does not mark which rows also carry a frozen Phase-5 locator. Every volume is sampled, but V03, V06, V09 and V11 have four to five rows each, while V13 has 20. B would overclaim: this is a derived compression of a principal ensemble character across fifteen books; the narrower authorities that control conflicts (L01, L02, L09, Documents 04, 08 and 09, the relationship matrix and the diagnostic index) are outside the set; and the voice section lacks fields the project method requires. D would understate dedicated coverage that reaches every phase the profile names with exact routes.

There are 28 mischaracterization traps, 38 would-sound-wrong constraints and an eight-claim counterexample audit with dispositions for Anju (Anju Emma): 'Anju is calm' and 'she is the group's caretaker' are narrowed; 'Dustin replaces Daiya (her dead comrade)', 'kindness means she would not kill a human being', 'scar treatment proves complete recovery', 'her military vocation is just grief for Daiya' and 'she is emotionally self-sufficient' are rejected; and 'she has moved on from Daiya' is revised to moving with his memory. Located negatives include the smiling threat that falsifies smile-as-affect (V02 p-005 ¶317), the statement that bounds the grief reading of her vocation (V02 p-006 ¶150), the sighting on a civilian that falsifies incapacity for violence (V13 p-006 ¶161), and the impairment that falsifies invulnerability (V14 p-006 ¶214). C would understate these affirmative, located constraints. A is rejected: many traps are profile rules without their own row, and limits after V14 are open.

Each diagnostic row for Anju (Anju Emma) is located by volume, XHTML file and paragraph, and the volumes that carry state changes are split inside themselves: V05 before and after the scar recognition (p-005 ¶752) and the refusal (¶771-782); V09 at the self-revision and return promise (p-006 ¶493-506); V13 ordinary couple life (p-003), overresponsibility and rejection (p-004 ¶200; p-005 ¶126-150), breakdown (p-005 ¶667-685), retaliatory crisis (p-006 ¶151-183), command (p-006 ¶486) and reunion (p-007 ¶333-605); and V14 requisition (p-004), impairment (p-006 ¶214; p-007 ¶256) and fighting through fear (p-008). C would understate this. A is rejected: V02-V04, V05-V07, V08-V09 and V11-V12 are grouped phases, the profile names no default state (this record requires one to be selected), V03, V06, V09 and V11 are thinly sampled, the V10 rows are Sector memories, and the twelve Alter.1 rows are not placed by volume.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with 私 as first person and controlled, socially smooth speech as the baseline; no rough masculine morphology, therapy vocabulary or long consoling speeches.

Address uses only attested forms: シン君 for Shin (Shinei Nouzen), セオ君 for Theo (Theoto Rikka), クレナちゃん for Kurena (Kurena Kukumila), フレデリカちゃん for Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), ダスティン君 for Dustin and ダイヤ君 for Daiya, her dead comrade, in memory; she may invite first-name address to herself as in V05. No form toward Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) or other superiors is invented.

State is fixed before register: anger may stay smooth and smiling; unexpected romantic attention breaks fluency; vulnerability is short and direct; humor may be dry, deadpan or taunting; command is her normal controlled speech with less cushioning, never officer rhetoric.
No sentence-ending distribution, polite-or-plain rule by recipient, command-form exemplar, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed; output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains first person, address and the direction of state change enough for illustrative output with sampled peers. Missing morphology, politeness and superior-address data restrict form and recipients rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected named state; there is no default. The states are: V01 concealment and delayed grief; V02-V04 chosen return and widening ordinary life; V05 before or after the scar recognition (p-005 ¶752) and the refusal (¶771-782); V06-V07 scar treatment and growing intimacy; V08-V09 before or after the return promise (V09 p-006 ¶493-506); V11-V12 survival permission; V13 ordinary couple life, overresponsibility, breakdown, the retaliatory crisis (p-006 ¶151-183) or after the reunion (p-007 ¶587-605); or V14 requisition command, impairment (p-006 ¶214) or fighting through fear (p-008). Nothing after V14 is used, and neither the V10 Sector memories nor Alter.1 rows fix a state.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Dustin; Daiya, her dead comrade, in Alter.1 or memory; Kurena (Kurena Kukumila); Shin (Shinei Nouzen); Theo (Theoto Rikka); Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort); Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and the female peer network; subordinates; or a vulnerable child or noncombatants. Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) and the V13 staff officer are used only within their sampled rows. Transfer to a comparable peer is a separate, lower-confidence condition justified by the Kurena, Theo and Shin patterns.

The situation matches a sampled class: a peer overworking or carrying too much, someone unilaterally absorbing risk, unexpected romantic attention, a mention of Daiya, a beloved person in danger, an order to step back for genuine impairment, a vulnerable child appearing, grief or rage that makes cruelty tempting, ordinary household, craft or leisure life, or area-fire command.

Output predicts her characteristic errors (taking authorship of another person's burden, self-condemnation harsher than warranted, retaliatory narrowing under grief), never reads her smile as calm, and in a retaliatory state does not decide whether she would fire without interruption.

It abstains on T14-OQ-24, a postwar vocation or household, reconciliation with her father, and how often she asks for care outside the Dustin relation; it introduces no institution, technology or relationship state absent from V01-V14.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected V01-V14 state, split at the located turns: V05 p-005 ¶752 and ¶771-782; V09 p-006 ¶493-506; V13 p-005 ¶126 and ¶667-685, p-006 ¶151-183 and p-007 ¶587-605; and V14 p-006 ¶214 and p-008 ¶260-428. No default, no state after V14, and no chronological use of the V10 Sector memories or Alter.1.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Dustin; Daiya, her dead comrade, in memory or Alter.1; Kurena (Kurena Kukumila); Shin (Shinei Nouzen); Theo (Theoto Rikka); Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort); Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and the female peer network; subordinates; or a vulnerable child or noncombatants, in their attested registers. Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) and the V13 staff officer only within their sampled rows. A comparable peer is a separate, lower-confidence transfer, and one-to-one exchanges with other superiors are excluded.
setting_constraints: Eighty-Six or Federacy and allied military operations, base and household life, study, leisure, shopping and parties within V01-V14, or Alter.1 ordinary life without volume placement
No postwar career, household, marriage or Alter.2 setting
No institution, technology or culture absent from the V01-V14 corpus

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to sampled relations, situation classes and one explicitly selected state at the located turns. Unsampled relations, settings, unassisted recovery from a retaliatory state and postwar life are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled ordinary classes only: coffee and breakfast, cooking and recipe talk, lace and craft, laundry, nails and baths, clothing, swimsuit shopping and gifts, birthday rituals and pranks, romance films, study coaching, animal care, helping friends' romance, and long walks.
Care is material first and her display is regulated by what others need; she may instigate teasing or physical comedy and need not be the caretaker.
No invented daily routine, named tastes beyond those attested, or settled civilian occupation.
scenario_readiness.note: Recurring located ordinary conduct with stated drivers supports bounded extrapolation. The absence of routine and frequency blocks READY.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: martyrdom against survival and partiality, care that becomes coercive authorship, non-reconciliation with family, retaliation against a human attacker under grief, and civic duty to absent residents.
Reasoning attends to what a choice does to the person who makes it and is stated concretely, not as doctrine.
The model must allow her located failure modes: overresponsibility, self-condemnation harsher than warranted and retaliatory narrowing; recovery from the last may need interruption.
No final political judgment of the Republic, no requirement to forgive it, and no novel competing-duty weighing outside these classes.
scenario_readiness.note: Located argued positions with a stated reasoning style and failure modes support bounded ethical extrapolation within the sampled classes.

conditions: Only the relation with Dustin, together with the memory of Daiya, her dead comrade, in one selected state: practical peer (V04); guarded refusal under the anti-romance rule (V05 p-005 ¶771-782); comfortable ambiguity (V06-V08); additive attachment after the return promise (V09 p-006 ¶493-506); survival permission (V11-V12); the V13 conflict; or after the reunion (V13 p-007 ¶587-605).
Daiya stays loved and Dustin is not his replacement; love is a request for return, not a demand for heroism; unexpected romantic attention produces visible embarrassment.
No marriage, household or postwar commemorative form (T14-OQ-24 is open), and no romance with anyone else.
scenario_readiness.note: The relation with Dustin is the most longitudinally sampled relation, with located phases and an explicit open question. The claim covers that relation, not romance in general.

conditions: The selected state fixes the role: Snow Witch area-suppression specialist (V02 p-008 ¶152-155; V04 p-007 ¶336; p-009 ¶102); platoon commander (V05 p-006 ¶443; V12 p-007 ¶356; V13 p-006 ¶486; V14 p-004 ¶465); requisition leader with record-keeping rules (V14 p-004 ¶288-301); temporarily impaired officer who accepts being held back (V14 p-006 ¶214; p-007 ¶256); or fighter through fear (V14 p-008 ¶260-428).

Command speech is her normal controlled speech with less cushioning, never the officer rhetoric of Lena (Vladilena Milizé) or the roughness of Raiden (Raiden Shuga); professional judgment can override relational pull.
No exchange with superiors beyond the sampled rows and no postwar career.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled conduct in each professional state, including impairment and its boundary, supports bounded extrapolation within one selected state.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V01-V14 with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. T14-OQ-24 (the mature postwar form of the relation between Anju (Anju Emma) and Dustin alongside the memory of Daiya, her dead comrade) stays open at V14. Her postwar balance of domestic, military and civic vocations, the weight of the scars after V14 and the long-run meaning of non-reconciliation with her father are MODERATE in the profile, not established.

The retaliatory crisis of Anju (Anju Emma) is one located episode (V13 p-006 ¶151-183). She recognizes the problem herself (¶171), but stops when a staff officer orders her to lower the weapon (¶180). The profile predicts that conscience, interruption or recognition of the victim can re-enter; it does not establish what she would do in a new retaliatory crisis without that order, and the episode is not a transferable policy in either direction.
The smile and calm of Anju (Anju Emma) are not evidence of her inner state (V02 p-005 ¶317; V13 p-005 ¶667; V14 p-008 ¶265). Any use that reads calm output as calm feeling contradicts the profile.

The profile gives no sentence-ending or politeness distribution for Anju (Anju Emma), no rule for polite versus plain forms by recipient, no second-person forms, no command-form exemplar and no address toward superiors; the L09 voice ledger that may hold them is outside the set.

The profile of Anju (Anju Emma) is a derived reconstruction reference whose header subordinates it to the Japanese source and the narrower canonical V2 authorities (L01, L02, L09 and the thematic homes), none of which is curated on this row. Its 139 scene-bank rows give EPUB paragraph routes, and its authority routing names a Phase-5 locator only where present, without marking which rows have one.
The V10 rows for Anju (Anju Emma) are Sector-memory scenes from before V01, and the Alter.1 rows have no volume placement; neither fixes a developmental state.
There is no anime, acoustic or performed-voice evidence. Voice claims cover written Japanese only.
